speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your symptoms. You mentioned postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; how long have you been experiencing these, and does the pain worsen with movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Regarding the "decrease in bowel sounds," were you specifically told this by a healthcare provider, or is this something you felt yourself? Additionally, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or have you had any bowel movements since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometritis with possible urinary tract involvement. The combination of postpartum fever, uterine tenderness, and urinary frequency is highly suggestive of endometritis, though decreased bowel sounds and urinary frequency could also indicate a urinary tract infection or constipation complicating the picture. Given the severity of symptoms, immediate evaluation is warranted.
